points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 1643年1月4日，牛顿出生于林肯郡伍尔索普的一个小农庄。他是个早产儿，父亲在他出生前就已去世。童年时期，牛顿表现出对机械装置的浓厚兴趣，制作了风车、水钟等小发明。1655年，他被送到格兰瑟姆文法学校学习，展现出非凡的智力。这段时期，牛顿开始对自然现象产生浓厚兴趣，尤其是日晷和风车等机械装置的制作，为他后来的科学研究奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Born on January 4, 1643, in Woolsthorpe, Lincolnshire, Newton was a premature child whose father had died before his birth. During his childhood, he showed a keen interest in mechanical devices, creating small inventions like windmills and water clocks. In 1655, he was sent to Grantham Grammar School where his exceptional intelligence became apparent. During this period, Newton developed a strong curiosity about natural phenomena, particularly the construction of mechanical devices like sundials and windmills, laying the foundation for his later scientific pursuits.

points.title: 求学剑桥
points.description: 1661年，牛顿进入剑桥大学三一学院学习，按照传统课程学习亚里士多德哲学。然而，他很快被新数学和自然科学所吸引，特别是笛卡尔的几何学和开普勒的天文学。1663年，学院建立了卢卡斯讲座，由巴罗教授担任首任教授，巴罗发现了牛顿的数学才能并给予指导。在剑桥期间，牛顿开始发展自己的数学理论，包括流数术（微积分的前身），并开始思考重力问题，为他后来万有引力定律的发现埋下伏笔。
points.descriptionEn: In 1661, Newton entered Trinity College, Cambridge, where he studied traditional Aristotelian philosophy. However, he quickly became fascinated by new mathematics and natural sciences, particularly Cartesian geometry and Kepler's astronomy. In 1663, the college established the Lucasian Professorship, with Isaac Barro as the first professor. Barro recognized Newton's mathematical talent and provided him with guidance. During his time at Cambridge, Newton began developing his own mathematical theories, including method of fluxions (precursor to calculus), and started contemplating the problem of gravity, laying the groundwork for his later discovery of the law of universal gravitation.

points.title: 奇迹之年
points.description: 1665年，剑桥因瘟疫关闭，牛顿返回伍尔索普的家中。这段时期被称为牛顿的'奇迹之年'，他在这里做出了多项重大发现：发展了微积分（流数术）、发现了光的色散现象、提出了万有引力定律的基本概念。据传，牛顿看到苹果从树上坠落，启发了他对重力本质的思考。在这18个月里，牛顿奠定了后来二十多年科学工作的基础，包括光学、运动定律和万有引力理论的核心思想。
points.descriptionEn: In 1665, due to the Great Plague, Cambridge University was closed, and Newton returned to his home in Woolsthorpe. This period, known as Newton's 'Annus Mirabilis' (Year of Miracles), saw him make several major discoveries: developing calculus (method of fluxions), discovering the phenomenon of light dispersion, and formulating the basic concepts of the law of universal gravitation. Legend has it that Newton's observation of an apple falling from a tree inspired his thoughts on the nature of gravity. During these 18 months, Newton laid the foundation for his scientific work over the next two decades, including core ideas on optics, laws of motion, and the theory of universal gravitation.

points.title: 学术巅峰
points.description: 1667年，牛顿返回剑桥，被选为三一学院研究员。1669年，他接替巴罗成为卢卡斯数学教授，在此职位上任职近30年。这一时期，牛顿完成了他的主要科学著作，包括《光学》和《自然哲学的数学原理》（1687年出版）。在《原理》中，他系统阐述了三大运动定律和万有引力定律，奠定了经典力学的基础。牛顿还改进了反射望远镜，并进行了大量光学实验。作为教授，他培养了多位杰出的数学家，包括年轻的天文学家哈雷。这一时期是牛顿科学成就最辉煌的阶段，他的工作彻底改变了人类对物理世界的理解。
points.descriptionEn: Returning to Cambridge in 1667, Newton was elected a Fellow of Trinity College. In 1669, he succeeded Barro as Lucasian Professor of Mathematics, a position he held for nearly 30 years. During this period, Newton completed his major scientific works, including 'Opticks' and 'Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica' (published in 1687). In the Principia, he systematically formulated his three laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation, establishing the foundation of classical mechanics. Newton also improved the reflecting telescope and conducted extensive optical experiments. As a professor, he mentored several outstanding mathematicians, including the young astronomer Edmond Halley. This period marked Newton's most brilliant scientific achievements, as his work fundamentally transformed humanity's understanding of the physical world.

points.title: 公职生涯
points.description: 1696年，牛顿移居伦敦，担任皇家铸币厂监督，1703年升任厂长。在此职位上，他改革了英国的货币体系，重新铸造了大量硬币，并严厉打击伪币制造者。1703年，牛顿当选为皇家学会会长，连任24年直至去世，对学会产生了深远影响。晚年，牛顿将更多精力投入到神学和炼金术研究中，撰写了大量相关著作。1727年3月31日，牛顿在伦敦肯辛顿去世，国葬于威斯敏斯特教堂，成为第一位获此殊荣的科学家。牛顿的公职生涯虽然远离科学研究，但他对英国科学和货币体系的贡献同样显著。
points.descriptionEn: In 1696, Newton moved to London to become Warden of the Royal Mint, and was promoted to Master in 1699. In this position, he reformed England's currency system, oversaw the recoinage of currency, and vigorously prosecuted counterfeiters. In 1703, Newton was elected President of the Royal Society, a position he held for 24 years until his death, profoundly influencing the society. In his later years, Newton devoted more energy to theological and alchemical research, writing numerous works on these subjects. On March 31, 1727, Newton died in Kensington, London, and was given a state funeral at Westminster Abbey, becoming the first scientist to receive such honor. Although Newton's public service took him away from scientific research, his contributions to British science and the monetary system were equally significant.

supporter.zh: 牛顿被科学界誉为最伟大的科学家之一，他的三大运动定律和万有引力定律彻底改变了人类对宇宙的理解。作为微积分的创始人之一，他提供了描述自然现象的数学工具。牛顿的科学方法强调实验验证和数学推理的结合，为现代科学奠定了方法论基础。他的《自然哲学的数学原理》被视为科学史上最具影响力的著作之一，其影响力持续了三个多世纪。牛顿不仅是一位科学家，还是一位杰出的实验家和理论家，他的工作代表了人类理性思维的巅峰。
supporter.en: Newton is regarded by the scientific community as one of the greatest scientists in history. His three laws of motion and law of universal gravitation revolutionized humanity's understanding of the universe. As a co-inventor of calculus, he provided mathematical tools for describing natural phenomena. Newton's scientific method, emphasizing the combination of experimental verification and mathematical reasoning, laid the foundation for modern scientific methodology. His 'Principia Mathematica' stands as one of the most influential works in scientific history, with its impact lasting over three centuries. Newton was not only a scientist but also an exceptional experimentalist and theoretician, whose work represents the pinnacle of human rational thought.

critic.zh: 牛顿的学术生涯也存在争议和局限性。他投入大量时间研究炼金术和神学，这些研究在现代看来缺乏科学依据。牛顿在光学领域的某些观点后来被证明是错误的，如他坚持光的粒子说而反对波动说。在科学优先权问题上，牛顿与胡克、莱布尼茨等人存在激烈争论，有时表现得不够宽容。此外，牛顿在铸币厂任职期间对伪币制造者的严厉镇压被一些人视为过于严苛。这些方面反映了牛顿作为历史人物的复杂性，以及科学发展的曲折性。
critic.en: Newton's academic career also contains controversies and limitations. He devoted significant time to alchemy and theological studies, which lack scientific basis by modern standards. Some of Newton's views in optics, such as his insistence on the particle theory of light while opposing the wave theory, were later proven incorrect. In matters of scientific priority, Newton engaged in fierce disputes with figures like Hooke and Leibniz, sometimes showing a lack of generosity. Additionally, Newton's harsh suppression of counterfeiters during his tenure at the Mint has been criticized by some as excessively severe. These aspects reflect the complexity of Newton as a historical figure and the曲折 nature of scientific progress.

objective.zh: 在历史学和流行文化中，牛顿常被塑造为科学革命的象征人物。他的'苹果坠落'故事成为科学发现最著名的轶事之一，象征着偶然观察与深刻洞察的结合。牛顿的形象超越了纯粹的科学家，代表着理性主义与启蒙精神的兴起。他的名言'如果我看得更远，那是因为我站在巨人的肩膀上'体现了科学传承的重要性。在当代，牛顿被视为科学方法的典范，他的工作不仅改变了科学，也影响了哲学、艺术和流行文化。牛顿的遗产包括科学成就、方法论贡献以及作为文化偶像的多重身份。
objective.en: In historiography and popular culture, Newton is often portrayed as a symbolic figure of the Scientific Revolution. His 'apple falling' story has become one of the most famous anecdotes about scientific discovery, symbolizing the combination of偶然 observation and profound insight. Newton's image transcends that of a mere scientist, representing the rise of rationalism and Enlightenment spirit. His famous quote 'If I have seen further, it is by standing on the shoulders of giants' reflects the importance of scientific inheritance. In contemporary contexts, Newton is regarded as a paradigm of scientific methodology, and his work has not only transformed science but also influenced philosophy, art, and popular culture. Newton's legacy encompasses his scientific achievements, methodological contributions, and his identity as a cultural icon.

self.zh: 如果我看得更远，那是因为我站在巨人的肩膀上。
self.en: If I have seen further, it is by standing on the shoulders of giants.

others.zh: 自然与自然规律都隐藏在黑暗之中，上帝说：让牛顿来吧！于是一切光明。
others.en: Nature and nature's laws lay hid in night; God said, Let Newton be! and all was light.
